summary: ICICI Bank provides accounts, loans, cards and business payment services, accessible through branches and digital channels such as iMobile.
description: A customer can receive a salary, pay a shop or borrow for a home through ICICI Bank. A business can use it to collect customer payments or finance stock. The bank runs these services, assesses borrowers and collects repayments while keeping money available for payments and withdrawals.
money: Loans and investments earn interest. Some banking services earn fees. The bank pays interest on deposits and other borrowing, runs branches and computer systems, and records costs for loans that may not be repaid. Neither a customer deposit nor the principal returned on a loan is ordinary sales income.
customers: Households and businesses pay for borrowing and relevant services. Savers place money in accounts and may receive interest. The bank also serves overseas Indians and larger companies with different payment and borrowing needs.
drivers: Reliable deposits, the difference between interest earned and paid, borrower repayments, service fees, running costs and the money needed to keep the bank financially strong.

groups.title: Accounts, deposits and payments
groups.examples: Savings and current accounts, fixed and recurring deposits, debit cards, transfers and iMobile.
groups.explanation: An account helps customers keep money, receive payments and pay others. An app is a way of using these services. Deposited money remains an amount owed to the customer under the account terms.

groups.title: Borrowing for household needs
groups.examples: Home, vehicle, education and personal loans, and credit cards.
groups.explanation: Customers receive money or credit now and repay under agreed terms. Some loans are backed by property the bank can seek to recover if repayments fail. Different loans carry different costs and risks.

groups.title: Business loans and trade services
groups.examples: Finance for stock and daily operations, business loans, collections and cross-border payments.
groups.explanation: A company may buy goods before its customers pay it. The bank can lend during that gap or help move and collect payments, earning interest or relevant fees.

groups.title: Investments and other financial products
groups.examples: Investment distribution, wealth services and wider group businesses.
groups.explanation: The bank may arrange a product supplied by another company or have an ownership stake in a financial business. Arranging a sale and owning that business are different ways of earning money.

basics.title: A loan brings income and a repayment risk
basics.text: Interest is the charge for using borrowed money. Returning the principal gives back the amount lent. If a borrower struggles, the bank may lose some principal as well as future interest.

basics.title: Deposits must remain repayable
basics.text: A customer’s account balance is an obligation of the bank. Loans can run for years, while some deposits can be withdrawn much sooner. The bank must manage both the cost of funding and when money has to be available.

steps.title: Bring in deposits and other funding
steps.text: Offer accounts and services customers use, and arrange other permitted borrowing when needed.

steps.title: Check ability to repay
steps.text: Assess a proposed borrower’s income, commitments and any pledged security, then agree the loan and repayment terms.

steps.title: Provide the service and collect
steps.text: Run accounts and payments, collect interest, fees and loan repayments, and pay interest and operating bills.

steps.title: Follow up difficulties and keep financial cushions
steps.text: Record provisions, meaning charges or allowances for possible loan losses. Keep capital to absorb losses and liquidity, meaning funds available to meet payments when due.

specifics.title: Net interest income comes before several costs
specifics.text: This means interest earned minus interest paid. Staff, technology, loan losses and tax still affect the final profit, along with fees and other income.

specifics.title: Writing off a loan is different from being repaid
specifics.text: A write-off removes a loan amount from the accounts under the applicable treatment; collection efforts may continue. A recovery means money actually comes back. A smaller reported problem-loan balance can therefore have several explanations.

specifics.title: More app use does not mean more fee income
specifics.text: Customers can make many digital transactions without each producing a fee. Technology also needs spending and safeguards. Read activity together with income and costs.

watch: Are deposits supporting lending at a sensible cost?
The bank has to fund loans while meeting withdrawals.
Read deposit types, interest paid, other borrowing and available funds alongside lending growth. A larger deposit total can still become more expensive.
Are borrowers keeping up with payments?
New lending may develop problems after it is made.
Read new problem loans, recoveries, write-offs and provisions together. Check both the amount of troubled lending and its proportion of all loans.
Why is the interest difference changing?
Deposit and loan rates do not all reset together.

Read lending rates, deposit costs and loan types. Net interest margin compares net interest income with a stated average amount of assets, such as loans and investments. Check that basis before comparing periods or banks.
Which services produce fees after their costs?
Transactions and customer registrations are activity measures.
Look at fee categories alongside staff and technology costs. Separate normal service income from gains on selling investments or other unusual events.
Does growth leave enough protection against losses and withdrawals?
Profit alone does not show the bank can safely keep expanding.
Read capital cushions and funds available for payments. Keep standalone bank accounts separate from consolidated accounts, which include controlled group companies.
risks: Household or business difficulties can cause losses, including on loans without pledged property.
Deposits cost more or move away
Competition and withdrawals can raise funding costs or restrict further lending.
Fraud, outages, cyber incidents and rule breaches can interrupt services and cause losses.
Interest rates and investment prices move
These can change the income earned, funding cost and value of investments at different times.
context: A jump in loans and deposits needs its explanation

ICICI Bank’s 17 October 2026 release for July–September 2026 reports a large rise in deposits and loans, and also gives slower growth figures that leave out FCNR(B) deposits and loans linked to them. FCNR(B) deposits are deposits kept in a foreign currency, such as US dollars, by Indians living abroad; the release links some loans made by the bank’s international branches to these deposits. Read the bank’s own breakdown before treating a jump as ordinary new borrowing by Indian households and businesses. The same release reports a small treasury loss—a loss from trading bonds and other investments—which is separate from income earned by serving customers.
quiz: If a bank writes off a loan, does that mean the borrower paid it back?
No. A write-off is an accounting action. Repayment or recovery brings money back. Read both when checking why reported problem loans changed.
sources: FY 2025–26 annual report filed with the SEC

financialNotes.title: Use bank measures on a consistent basis
financialNotes.text: The audited figures cover the consolidated group, including insurance businesses. Gross total income, net interest income and profit after tax measure different stages of the business. Deposits, advances and assets are balance-sheet amounts. The table does not allocate profit to each card, account or loan product.
